source_caption:
The first teaser for Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three has officially arrived. Adapted from Frank Herbert's 1969 novel Dune Messiah, the epic conclusion picks up 12 years after the events of Part Two, following Paul Atreides as he grapples with the devastating consequences of the holy war waged in his name and the growing conspiracies threatening to dismantle his reign. Villeneuve shot the film over the course of a five-month production in Budapest and Abu Dhabi, with select sequences captured on IMAX cameras. Building on a franchise that has earned over $1.12 billion worldwide and eight Academy Awards across its first two installments, Part Three is shaping up to be the most ambitious chapter yet. The epic conclusion arrives December 18, 2026. Denis Villeneuve calls it a "thriller," more action-packed than the first two films, set 17 years after Part Two. Shot primarily on 65mm film with select sequences in 15/70mm IMAX, while desert scenes were captured in IMAX digital.

source_details.synopsis: Dune: Part Three is an upcoming epic space opera film directed by Denis Villeneuve, from a screenplay he wrote with Brian K. Vaughan. Based on the Dune novels by Frank Herbert, it is the sequel to Dune: Part Two (2024) and the third of a trilogy of films developed by Legendary Pictures. Villeneuve produced the film with his wife and business partner Tanya Lapointe, Legendary's Mary Parent and Cale Boyter, and Joseph M. Caracciolo Jr. Timothée Chalamet leads an eleven-actor cast as Paul Atreides, a despotic emperor forced to contend with the fallout of his ascent to the throne, including threats of an insurgency and visions of widespread pandemonium.
